title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the neighbouring pages 656 and 658. G^+ is a profinite group with distinguished elliptic elements rho and sigma, where mu = {1, rho^3} = {1, sigma^2} is central. This is plausibly the profinite completion of SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. It also has a distinguished 'cusp/loop' element epsilon_0, and L_0 = {epsilon_0^n, n in Z^} is the corresponding procyclic subgroup. 𝔊 is a subgroup of G^+, with test cases 𝔊 = pi and 𝔊 = pi_0. Z_{rho,sigma} is a group of quadruples (u, mu, eps2, eps3) with u in Aut(G^+), mu in Z^*, and eps2, eps3 in {±1}. The conditions are: (a) u(rho) is 𝔊-conjugate to rho^{eps3}; (b) u(sigma) is 𝔊-conjugate to sigma^{eps2}; (c) u(epsilon_0) = epsilon_0^mu; (d) u stabilises 𝔊, possibly with further conditions on the action on G^+/𝔊. It is a 'Teichmüller-type' symmetry group of the profinite modular group: automorphisms preserving the elliptic conjugacy classes up to 𝔊-conjugacy and the cusp generator up to a cyclotomic exponent.

The page opens by finishing a remark from p. 656. In the universal case, u(rho) is conjugate in G^+ to rho^{eps3}, but in general not by elements of pi. Hence, when one wants conjugation by elements of the small group, one must restrict to eps3 = 1, since rho^{-1} ≠ rho.

Definitions on the page:
- (18) L_0^𝔊 := {l in L_0 | (int(l), 1, 1, 1) in Z_{rho,sigma}}. These are the powers of the cusp generator whose inner automorphisms satisfy the defining conditions.
- (19) The canonical homomorphism i: L_0^𝔊 → Z_{rho,sigma}, l ↦ (int_{G^+}(l), 1, 1, 1).
- (20) i is injective iff L_0^𝔊 ∩ Centre(G^+) = {1}.
- The image is normal ('invariante'). Indeed, for z = (u, mu, …) in Z one has u ∘ int(l) ∘ u^{-1} = int(u(l)) = int(l^mu), and l^mu is again in L_0^𝔊.
- (21) Gamma_{rho,sigma} := Z_{rho,sigma} / L_0^𝔊.
- (22) This gives the exact sequence 1 → L_0^𝔊 → Z → Gamma → 1.
- (23) The characters eps3, chi (= mu) and eps2 of Z are trivial on the image of L_0^𝔊, so they descend to characters eps3γ: Gamma → mu, chiγ: Gamma → Z^*, eps2γ: Gamma → mu.
- (24), begun here and rewritten cleanly on p. 658: the index-2 kernels Gamma' = Ker eps3γ, Gamma'' = Ker eps2γ, Gamma''' = Ker(eps2γ · eps3γ), and their inverse images Z', Z'', Z''' in Z.

Marginal NB: L_0^𝔊 ⊇ L_0 ∩ 𝔊, and the inclusion can be strict. Example: L_0^𝔊 = L_0^pi while L_0 ∩ 𝔊 = L_0^{pi_0}.

Purpose: to divide out the 'trivial' symmetries coming from conjugation by the cusp element. This is the usual normalisation ambiguity of a tangential base point. The resulting quotient Gamma_{rho,sigma} is a GT-like group with cyclotomic character chi. The next page builds semidirect products Z·G^+ and Z·G^natural and an embedding of L_0 into them.
errors: Injectivity criterion (20) is correct but essentially automatic in the main example. If G^+ is the profinite SL2(Z), its centre is {±1}, and no nontrivial power epsilon_0^n with n in Z^ is central, so the intersection is trivial. Grothendieck states it as a condition, presumably for general 𝔊 or G^+.

The containment L_0 ∩ 𝔊 ⊆ L_0^𝔊 in the NB tacitly needs int(l) to stabilise 𝔊 (condition d). This is automatic when l ∈ 𝔊, so the claim is fine. Whether it stays fine depends on the extra conditions on the action on G^+/𝔊, which Grothendieck is still revising on pp. 656–658 (he later writes 'c'est mauvais').

The defining conditions of Z_{rho,sigma} are visibly unstable across these pages: the marginal modifications of (14) and condition (d), and the later self-criticism on p. 658. The objects on this page are therefore provisional.

ideas.what: Quotienting a group of 'conjugacy-class-preserving' automorphisms (u, chi, eps2, eps3) of a profinite modular group by inner automorphisms coming from the cusp subgroup L_0, giving Gamma_{rho,sigma} = Z/L_0^𝔊.
ideas.modern_name: Normalising away inner automorphisms by the tangential-base-point (cusp) stabiliser in the definition of GT-type groups; analogue of passing from automorphisms to outer automorphisms relative to the inertia/cusp subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps for GT; genus-one / modular analogues by Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Enriquez (elliptic GT)
ideas.where_published: The general programme of a Teichmüller-type 'tower' group is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific construction is not known to be published

ideas.what: Characters eps2, eps3 (signs on the elliptic generators) and chi (cyclotomic exponent on the cusp) of the symmetry group, and their index-2 kernels Gamma', Gamma'', Gamma'''.
ideas.modern_name: Sign/cyclotomic characters of a GT-type group for SL2(Z^)

ideas.what: Distinction between L_0 ∩ 𝔊 and the possibly larger L_0^𝔊 of cusp powers whose conjugation satisfies the defining conditions.
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser-type enlargement of the cusp subgroup

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a family of GT-like groups Gamma_{rho,sigma} attached to subgroups 𝔊 of the profinite modular group. They come with sign characters on the elliptic generators and a cyclotomic character on the cusp, and their structure (index-2 subgroups, extensions by L_0) is left uncomputed here. Comparing these groups with modern 'modular' or 'elliptic' GT groups, and with Aut/Out of profinite SL2(Z) preserving cusp data, appears not to have been carried out in exactly this form.
missed.quote: On pose (21) γ_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}/L_0^𝔊 ... déduits de (u, μ, ε_2, ε_3)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor but concrete variant of the 'GT for the modular tower' question. It would be of interest to people studying Out(SL2(Z)^) and genus-one GT-type groups; it is modest and likely subsumed by known frameworks.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine group-theoretic bookkeeping steps (quotient by cusp inner automorphisms, descended characters, index-2 kernels) inside a provisional, still-being-revised definition. The broader programme is known in spirit from the Esquisse and from GT literature.
transcription_corrections: The quotient group is written with a gamma-like letter (γ_{ρ,σ}, as on p. 658); 'Γ' in the transcription is a normalisation of this.

In (18) the right-hand side was first crossed out and the set {l ∈ L_0 | (int(l),1,1,1) ∈ Z_{ρ,σ}} added above. The parenthesis reads 'où L_0 ⊂ G^+ est l'ens des ε_0^n, n ∈ Ẑ', so the l on the right-hand side ranges over L_0 (without superscript 𝔊).
(19): the arrow is labelled 'i' and the map is l ↦ (int_{G^+}(l), 1, 1, 1).
(24) on this page is struck through and rewritten on p. 658.
Margin NB reads approximately: 'On a L_0^𝔊 ⊃ L_0 ∩ 𝔊 et l'inclusion peut être stricte, cf exemple ... ci-dessus où L_0^𝔊 = L_0^π, L_0 ∩ 𝔊 = L_0^{π_0}'.
